editorial.headline: An Apotek Activity Open Nationally—and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This code covers the pharmacy retail sale of human pharmaceutical preparations and specified health goods, with full national foreign-ownership availability and no Bali moratorium block recorded.
editorial.body:
An apotek operating under this activity is a retail setting for human pharmaceutical preparations in their many practical forms: tablets, capsules, ointments, powders, solutions, parenteral solutions and suspensions. The stated range is broad within that pharmacy setting, spanning preparations for skin, eye, dental, ear, respiratory and digestive conditions, high blood pressure and hormone disorders, alongside vitamins and health supplements. The defining point is not simply the product catalogue, but its retail sale through an apotek.

The scope also includes specified health-related goods made of rubber. These include condoms, breast pumps, feeding teats, blood bags, surgical gloves, rubber pipettes, family-planning devices and rubber stoppers for small pharmaceutical vials. Taken together, the activity describes a pharmacy retail operation able to handle both medicinal preparations for human use and the named health necessities that sit alongside them. It is open to businesses at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is recorded as TERBUKA for PMA, with maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In other words, the national record allows foreign ownership to reach the full ceiling stated for this activity. Its stated availability across every listed business scale gives the code a consistent national footing, from Mikro through Besar, rather than reserving it to one end of the scale spectrum.

Bali requires its own reading, because the province permanently blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA registration across the island. This activity is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. Bali marks it as OK or higher risk, and the record notes that, at Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The practical conclusion from the record is therefore clear: a foreign-owned apotek retail business under this activity is nationally open up to 100% foreign ownership, and it is not barred from PMA registration in Bali by the stated moratorium.
